references.text: The context of the law concerning the Hebrew female slave who shall not go free as male slaves do
Continuation of the laws regarding the rights of a female slave if her master fails to fulfill his obligations
The law on the redemption of Israelites who have sold themselves, including the right to be bought back
Prohibition against selling a woman taken in war if her husband no longer wants her, parallel to the prohibition against selling her to foreigners
Nehemiah mentions the Jews redeeming their brothers and sisters who had been sold to pagans
Related law concerning a man who seduces a virgin and the father's right to refuse the marriage
Both verses define the woman as a person with protected status in an intermediate stage (betrothed but not yet released), limiting men's rights over her.
